ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence for politically exposed persons, family members and close associates under Chapter 3 of the Law of 12 November 2004 (Articles 30-41) and CSSF Regulation 12-02; continuous screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (including EU Regulation 269/2014 and EU Regulation 833/2014), OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK HMT sanctions, and Luxembourg domestic designations issued by the High-Level Committee for Financial Action; the ISIC 3011 commercial shipyard profile is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, requiring independent verification of UBO identity, source of wealth, commercial rationale, and transaction purpose prior to name clearance and RBE filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS e-filing portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal form suffix must read 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'; the name may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, or any other language using the Latin alphabet and must be transliterable into French/Luxembourgish for RCS indexing; the name must contain a distinctive element and must not create confusion with existing registered names under Article 18 of the Law of 19 December 2002; names contrary to public order or suggesting misleading official status are prohibited.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (prior CSSF authorization required)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization required)
Fonds d'investissement / UCI / SIF / SICAV / SICAR (CSSF licensing and supervision regime applicable)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Clearing House / Central Depository (licensed financial infrastructure connotation)
État / Gouvernement / Luxembourg State / Administration communale (names implying state or public authority sponsorship)
Université / École / Académie (education-sector ministerial consent required)
Réviseur d'entreprises / Audit / Auditeur (regulated profession; statutory approval of Institut des Réviseurs d'Entreprises required)
Agréé / Autorisé / Licencié / Certifié (tokens implying official approval unless the corresponding license already exists)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection by the LBR registrar, the applicant must file a unilateral petition (requête unilatérale) before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) within one month of notification, pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 and Article 1078-1 of the New Code of Civil Procedure; the petition must attach the registrar's refusal, the proposed corporate name, and the certificate of availability; a single administrative extension of the reservation period may be sought through the LBR e-file portal, although extension is discretionary and the name remains unprotected until the full incorporation dossier is validated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted by the RCS for a purely holding or non-regulated SCSp provided the registered office is a physical street address in Luxembourg and the written consent of the occupant is filed; a virtual office will not satisfy commercial substance requirements for an ISIC 3011 shipyard entity manufacturing or operating ocean container vessels in Luxembourg, and such structures face challenge by the Administration des douanes et accises, the Luxembourg tax authorities, and CSSF where fund-linked activity is present; actual operating premises, staff, and vessel-yard capacity are mandatory if shipyard operations are conducted in the jurisdiction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high for the operating shipyard profile: approximately 30% estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Luxembourg authorities (Administration des douanes et accises, social security inspectorate, municipal licensing officers, and tax compliance visits) within a 24-month period; a passive SCSp used solely for financing and chartering, without Luxembourg operational premises, carries a lower inspection likelihood of 10-15%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Law of 12 July 2013 on the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp); RCS registration provisions (Commercial Code Book I, Title II)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Luxembourg Business Registers – LBR); RCS desk of the Luxembourg District Court
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statements and Articles of Partnership (Contrat de société and Déclaration commune) filed as the incorporation deed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital, no mandatory paid-up capital, and no escrow deposit requirement; the partners are free to determine capital contributions in the partnership agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding general partner adopts and subscribes to the initial partnership quota of the SCSp as set forth in the draft contribution schedules; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at 18 Rue des Bains, L-1212 Luxembourg, and that the authorised representative be instructed to execute the notarized deed, register the entity with the Luxembourg Business Registers, and publish the required legal notice; RESOLVED, that Mr. Laurent Schmitt be appointed as designated manager (Gérant) with full authority to open bank accounts, execute maritime installment LCs, and act before all administrative and industrial licensing authorities; all powers conferred under the Special Limited Partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request via LBR online services, indicating the intended corporate name, ISIC 3011 business scope, and jurisdiction. The registry will verify name distinctiveness against existing Luxembourg entities and protected trade names. The applicant receives a certificate of name clearance, which remains valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Notarized or apostilled passport copy of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, submit a revised name or file an appeal with the Registrar within eight business days, attaching evidence of prior use or trademark rights in Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary in Luxembourg or private deed with defined apostille
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding general partner and initial limited partner execute the partnership agreement containing SCSp name, registered office, capital contributions, profit sharing, transfer restrictions, and governance clauses. For shipyard activities, the deed must include an express object clause covering design, construction, repair, and fitting-out of deep-sea container vessels. The deed is executed by private signing with legalization or notarized if the SCSp will hold real estate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary or registry may add a rectification deed if clauses conflict with Luxembourg mandatory law; re-execution can be done within one week with curative clauses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Initial Contributions and Escrow Arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or payment services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although no minimum capital is statutorily required, the partnership agreement may stipulate initial cash contributions. If escrow is used for the shipyard, open an escrow account at an authorised Luxembourg bank, execute the escrow agreement, transfer subscribed cash into the account, and obtain a bank attestation for the RCS file confirming receipts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of subordinated loans, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays, the partners may make the capital contribution at a notary’s separate account, or amend the contribution schedule to a future call following a cured bank review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration file to LBR/RCS electronically, including executed partnership agreement, bank capital certificate, manager consent, registered office domiciliation consent, and beneficial-owner filing. The RCS registers the SCSp under a single identification number and issues the certificate of registration that evidences legal existence.
required_dossiers: Bank confirmation of contribution or escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried, LBR sends a notice of query; the filer must cure within ten business days via the online platform, including supplementary apostilles or corrected signatures, otherwise the application lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium and Appointment Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RESA – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the court clerk arranges publication of the mandatory corporate extracts in RESA. The manager then applies for a certificate of good standing and full extracts from RCS for opening the operational bank account and preparing the shipyard licensing applications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed due to technical issues, submit a direct request to the RCS registry for an expedited publication order; any error in the published extract must be corrected by a rectification filing within seven business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Établissement classé – Industrial Shipyard Operating Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Luxembourg Environment Agency – Administration de l’Environnement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A1 – Full EIA Report required for commercial shipbuilding and ship repair yards with docking facilities and metal fabrication
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Luxembourg water protection thresholds (≤0.1 mg/L free chlorine in treated discharge, VOC exhaust treatment BREF requirements under EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU), waste management under Waste Management Law of 21 March 2012, and noise emission limits per Grand-Ducal Regulation on noise in classified establishments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by Corps Grand-Ducal d’Incendie et de Secours, structural load inspection by the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works for dry-dock and slipway structures, and workplace clearance by Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) covering occupational health, machinery, welding gases, worker exposure, and emergency access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified e-government portal: MyGuichet (myguichet.lu), guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity may obtain a Luxembourg business number (matricule) and national tax ID by filing its partnership deed with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) through a Luxembourg registered office agent, followed by VAT registration with the AEDT on Form 700 via the MyGuichet platform. If the entity has no Luxembourg establishment but makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg, it must apply directly for a VAT identification number to the AEDT VAT department, using Form 700 and appointing a Luxembourg tax representative where required. Once registered, the entity receives a matricule and a VAT number (LU plus eight digits), which are used for filing VAT returns and recapitulative statements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent under Luxembourg law; no partnership-level corporate income tax classification election is available. Partners may elect, within their own jurisdictions, to apply look-through or check-the-box treatment. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD 1 and 2, transposed in 2019-2020) restrict outcomes where a hybrid entity obtains disproportionate deductions or non-inclusion. VAT grouping election under Article 60 LVD allows a fiscal unity for VAT purposes if all legal conditions are satisfied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-business exemption: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excluding real estate); no registration threshold for non-established foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg; OSS distance-selling threshold EUR 35,000 for non-established EU suppliers; B2B reverse charge applies where the customer is a Luxembourg VAT-registered business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping regime currently applies in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is permitted; Peppol BIS 3.0 is mandatory for invoices to Luxembourg central public authorities. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically via the MyGuichet portal (AEDT). Continuous transaction controls are planned but not yet in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations are zero-rated under Article 42 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (LVD), provided the goods are physically removed from the EU within the legal deadline (generally three months, extendable to six months) and documentary evidence of export is retained. Supply, repair, chartering or modification of ocean-going vessels used in international seafaring may be exempt or zero-rated under Article 43 LVD. For shipyard export of new container vessels, the supplier must be in possession of the export declaration, transport documents, and proof of payment to maintain zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic AES export declaration)
Bill of Lading (or sea waybill / through bill of lading, evidencing carriage to a destination outside the EU)
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT/MT103 proof of foreign payment
Commercial invoice, packing list and export delivery note
Certificate of non-EU destination / Form A or EUR.1 where preferential origin is claimed (as applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may audit zero-rated export transactions and will disallow the zero rate if the documentary evidence is incomplete, false or not presented within the statutory period. Consequences include immediate assessment of the unpaid VAT at the standard rate, statutory default interest (currently 5% per annum), and administrative fines under Article 87 LVD of up to 100% of the evaded VAT in cases of intentional concealment. Criminal penalties under Article 90 LVD may be imposed for fraud, including imprisonment. Retrospective clawbacks are permitted for up to five years, or ten years in cases of fraud, under Luxembourg tax procedure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank and operates within the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism alongside the European Central Bank (ECB). Foreign-exchange and cross-border capital-movement oversight is shared between the BCL, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance, and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which supervises credit institutions, payment institutions, and exchange-related licensing under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital-account and current-account convertibility are fully liberalised: Luxembourg, as a euro-area member, has eliminated all exchange-control restrictions for residents and non-residents under Articles 63–65 TFEU and the Luxembourg implementing legislation. Profit remittance and distribution hurdles are de minimis; an SCSp generally may remit partner distributions, loan repayments, and sale proceeds without prior central-bank approval, subject only to standard CSSF anti-money-laundering verification, ECB balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and tax-compliance filings confirming the pass-through character of the partnership. There is no separate capital-export licensing regime for shipbuilding project finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Eurozone law imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation requirement for export proceeds. Shipbuilding export receivables held by the SCSp can be retained in EUR, USD, or any third currency in Luxembourg and offshore correspondent accounts, subject to purely informational reporting: EU Regulation 2015/847 funds-transfer data rules (threshold EUR 1,000), ECB/BCL balance-of-payments declarations for transactions above EUR 12,500, and standard CSSF suspicious-transaction reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury rail; MEDIUM only as an ancillary payment channel for small disbursements. A Luxembourg-authorised or EU/EEA-passported Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under PSD2 cannot perform the core treasury functions of this mandate: it may not take deposits as a credit institution, may not issue commercial letters of credit, may not enter into ISDA-documented FX derivatives, and is structurally unable to host maritime installment escrow arrangements. Offshore digital EMIs located outside the EEA face a further legal constraint: unlicensed non-EEA payment providers cannot lawfully solicit Luxembourg entities, and large correspondent banks will reject all nostro traffic from such intermediaries. Capital escrow, LC issuance, and FX hedging must therefore remain exclusively with CSSF-licensed credit institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CSSF Circular 12/552 and the transposed EU 5AMLD framework technically permit risk-based remote onboarding with high-assurance video identification, but Luxembourg commercial practice reserves this option for low-risk retail clients. For a Medium-Risk-Enhanced commercial shipyard entity controlled by non-resident partners, all Tier-1 banks will require either (i) a physical interview in Luxembourg of the SCSp's general partner or a formally authorised Luxembourg-resident manager, or (ii) a secure virtual interview followed by notarisation and apostille of the full KYC file. Remote-only opening is effectively unavailable for accounts intended to operate documentary credits, escrow, and derivatives; the physical-presence interview is the presumptive mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA ultimate beneficial ownership combined with an SCSp's deliberate absence of a public beneficial-owner register and general-partner opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled UBO declaration (RBE/RCU-UBO form), a full organisational chart tracing each limited partner through intermediate entities to individual human UBOs, an extract of the SCSp partnership agreement containing the capital-account clause, passport copies, proof of residential address for each UBO, and a sworn Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the substance and commercial reality of the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag triggered by multi-million-euro ship construction instalments, freight-related back-to-back payments, and invoices issued before physical delivery.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial file: executed shipbuilding contract with phase-gated milestone schedule, commercial pro-forma invoices, shipyard production and procurement plans, purchase orders for marine engines and steel plate, triennial financial projections, independent valuation of the hull and equipment under construction, H&M and P&I insurance certificates, and a letter of comfort from the classification society (e.g., Bureau Veritas, DNV, or ABS) confirming the construction programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank's tax-transparency review characterising the SCSp as a pass-through shell that could mask dividend or capital flows from non-resident partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax ruling or confirmation letter from the Luxembourg Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA recognising the pass-through status under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, CRS/FATCA registration extracts, audited financial statements, substance dossier evidencing local payroll, board and partner meeting minutes, and a legal opinion citing the contractual autonomy of the société en commandite spéciale regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime sanctions exposure: vessel customers, ports of call, or beneficial owners linked to jurisdictions under UN/EU/OFAC restrictions or IMO shadow-fleet registries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening outputs against EU, UN, OFAC, and UK HMT lists generated at onboarding and every subsequent week; end-user and end-use attestation including IMO dual-use compliance clauses; vessel registration abstracts from a recognised maritime registry; a copy of the company's written EU Maritime Sanctions compliance policy; and a Wolfsberg-aligned trade-based money-laundering prevention manual covering the full invoice-to-delivery trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident partners inject equity via SWIFT MT103 wires denominated in EUR or USD. The instructing bank must reference the ECB Balance-of-Payments functional category F.61 (Direct investment – equity) or F.62 (Reinvestment of earnings), and the receiving Luxembourg bank requires the SCSp subscription agreement, the capital-call notice number, and a purpose-code description such as 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – LU SCSp / SHIPYARD EQUITY'. CSSF AML rules require identification of beneficial owners for every transfer above EUR 10,000; where the remitter is a corporate in a high-risk jurisdiction, the defence package must include proof of funds: audited financial statements, source-of-wealth statement, and transaction rationale. No mandatory conversion applies; the Luxembourg account may be credited in original currency and the SCSp may open segregated USD sub-accounts for subsequent shipbuilding disbursements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Shipyard milestone payments and trade settles through four regulated rails: (i) standard operational disbursements via SWIFT MT103/MT202 through BGL BNP Paribas and BIL correspondent chains; (ii) milestone payments under a Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit issued per UCP 600 with a confirmed Luxembourg advising bank; (iii) standby letters of credit (ISP98) and advance-payment/refund guarantees issued under URDG 758 in favour of shipowners and equipment vendors; and (iv) documentary collections under URC 522 for progress invoices. All EUR payments may alternatively clear through SEPA; USD payments clear via Fedwire/CHIPS through the banks' New York correspondents. Drawings are permitted only against compliant presentations: signed sea-trial certificates, classification-society survey reports, engine-room handover protocols, and clean commercial invoices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright OTC EUR/USD FX forward documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a MiFID II-licensed Luxembourg credit institution, permitted without restriction because the euro is fully deliverable.
EUR/USD cross-currency swap for long-dated shipyard milestone hedging, subject to EMIR clearing and margining requirements where applicable.
FX swap (spot versus forward) for intra-month working-capital rotation between EUR receivables and USD payable commitments.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing restricted or illiquid third-currency exposures (e.g., USD/CNY or USD/INR) only if the Luxembourg bank maintains an authorised non-deliverable desk and the transaction passes CSSF suitability, EMIR margin, and sanctions screens; NDFs are unnecessary for EUR crosses.
Exchange-traded FX futures executed on EU-regulated venues (e.g., Eurex) as an alternative clearing-house-backed hedge preserving the SCSp's credit capacity at the Tier-1 bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (declaration de confirmation annuelle au registre des beneficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 March of each calendar year; any change in beneficial ownership, including transfers of partnership interests, must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,250 for late or incomplete confirmation; deliberate omission may trigger criminal fines up to EUR 12,500 and imprisonment up to five years; RBE may also suspend the delivery of certificates of good standing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.note: For an SCSp, the general partner or its authorised Luxembourg service provider must maintain an up-to-date schedule of limited partners and ultimate beneficial owners and submit the annual confirmation through the RBE online portal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS e-storage service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 8 months of the financial year-end; for a December year-end, filing must be completed by 31 August of the following year. Extension by court order of up to 3 months is possible upon application.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs administrative complaints from the RCS, potentially followed by judicial summons and fines up to EUR 5,000; repeated default may prevent the issue of an RCS certificate and expose the general partner to enforcement measures.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.note: An SCSp is generally exempt from the obligation to file annual accounts because it lacks separate legal personality. Filing becomes mandatory if the entity voluntarily opts for publication or if all general partners are Luxembourg corporate entities subject to RCS filing requirements; investors often require audited accounts as a contractual matter.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual register verification and statutory records certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office service provider or Luxembourg corporate administrator; no direct filing to a public registry is required unless an inconsistency is discovered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately after the annual accounts closing date and before the UBO annual confirmation deadline, ordinarily within 3 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and verify statutory registers does not carry a specific financial penalty for an SCSp, but incorrect register entries may invalidate the partnership's proof of record for anti-money-laundering inspections and expose the general partner to disciplinary sanctions by the CSSF or the Ordre des Experts-Comptables.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.note: The review must cover the register of associates, minutes of partners' meetings, notarial deeds or private partnership agreements, and the chronological record of transfers of partnership interests.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For Luxembourg commercial undertakings, an independent statutory audit is required when two of the following three thresholds are exceeded on a non-consolidated basis: balance sheet total exceeds EUR 4,400,000; net turnover exceeds EUR 8,800,000; average number of full-time employees exceeds 50. An SCSp is not automatically captured by this requirement because it has no separate legal personality and is tax transparent, but auditing becomes compulsory if the SCSp publishes annual accounts voluntarily, is part of a consolidated group subject to Luxembourg law, or is expressly designated as a grand enterprise in the partnership agreement or by a regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial companies and annual accounts is the default statutory framework. IFRS as adopted by the EU may be applied on a voluntary basis, and it is mandatory for consolidated financial statements of listed entities and certain financial services undertakings. For a non-filing SCSp, internal financial statements are prepared at the instruction of the general partner, usually following Luxembourg GAAP with or without IFRS adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain a complete and current schedule of its direct and indirect beneficial owners. Every transfer of a partnership interest obliges the general partner to file a corrective UBO declaration with the Luxembourg RBE within 30 days and to re-confirm the entire register by the subsequent 31 March annual confirmation deadline. The annual confirmation may be submitted solely by the general partner or a delegated professional with a Luxembourg power of attorney; the system will generate a final confirmation receipt to be archived with the statutory books.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors or Managers (Register des gerants, if applicable)
Minute Book of partner and/or management resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 per annum for a standard registered office, administrative support, and corporate secretarial services provided by a licensed Luxembourg trust or company service provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000 - USD 48,000 per annum for a compliant independent audit of an SCSp with a shipyard investment holding profile; no audit fee is incurred if the SCSp remains exempt and the partnership agreement does not require an audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined rate: 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, and 6.75% municipal business tax; SCSp itself is fiscally transparent so no entity-level tax and allocations are taxable in the partners' hands)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is structurally exempt from Luxembourg corporate income tax; qualifying corporate partners may benefit from the participation exemption (0% WHT on dividends), IP box (80% exemption of qualifying IP income), 50% super-deduction for qualified R&D expenditure, and a tonnage tax regime for qualifying ship-owning/operating affiliates; no general shipyard tax holiday exists. Luxembourg law generally permits indefinite loss carryforward subject to an annual offset cap, but the fixed template field is populated as 5.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 200 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) for the SCSp's fiscal transparency statement, filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration e-filing portal); partners receive and attach the allocation schedule to their own corporate or individual returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a separate return is due for each financial period (no quarterly corporate returns for SCSp; withheld payroll/VAT may require specific quarterly filings).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal period ending 31 December, the return must be filed no later than 31 December of the following calendar year (12 months after fiscal year-end); subject to the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration's published e-filing extension rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp: registered corporate number (RCS), legal form, registered office, and status as a tax-transparent special limited partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure the SCSp enters the partnership's Luxembourg RCS and each partner's country of tax residence; no Luxembourg business licence number is required for pure holding/transparent structures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements result for the fiscal year: revenue from shipbuilding, cost of sales, operating expenses, depreciation, and provisions before allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may use the allocated share directly in their home-country return; attach a GAAP-compliant profit and loss statement signed by the general partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit/loss among partners, including the share attributable to each limited partner's capital account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert each non-resident partner's name, address, domicile, fiscal identification number, and exact allocation percentage; a missing allocation may make the SCSp taxable at the 24.94% corporate regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward and any special deductions (IP box, R&D super-deduction, notional interest deduction if available) claimed at the transparent entity level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot claim Luxembourg IP box or R&D super-deduction on allocable income unless they have a Luxembourg permanent establishment and maintain supporting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax haven or controlled foreign corporation disclosures, cross-border transactions, and DTA-related items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all related-party transactions (vessel construction, procurement, royalty, and interest flows) and attach tax residence certificate (TRC) if a treaty reduction is claimed at source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic fiscal penalty of up to 10% of the net tax due and monthly late-payment interest of 0.8%; repeated non-filing can lead to an ex parte assessment, loss of Tax Clearance Certificate, and criminal sanctions for the general partner.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard statutory rate for Luxembourg-source dividends paid to non-residents; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive/participation exemption when the 10% participation and 12-month holding conditions are satisfied; SCSp profit distributions to limited partners are generally not treaty-protected because the SCSp is tax transparent and no withholding is levied at partnership level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a treaty-reduced rate, the non-resident beneficiary must obtain an original or certified tax residence certificate (TRC) in the jurisdiction of residence, supply it to the Luxembourg withholding agent before payment, and, where applicable, submit the Luxembourg 'Application for withholding tax relief / refund' via MyGuichet.lu; relief at source is granted only if the Luxembourg tax office confirms the beneficial ownership and active substance of the recipient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg levies 0% withholding tax on cross-border royalty and interest payments at statutory level; treaty rates are therefore irrelevant for most outbound flows but a valid TRC should nevertheless be retained to support arm's-length characterisation and avoid recharacterisation as deferred dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is mandatory when Luxembourg consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds EUR 100,000,000; Local File is mandatory when the Luxembourg entity has cross-border related-party transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 and total turnover above EUR 10,000,000; lower thresholds apply if the group operates in highly digitalised or intangibles-intensive sectors.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply the Gulf-Cooperation Council style ESR, but the general anti-abuse rule, the OECD key-substance requirement under DTA/BEPS, and the EU ATAD require the SCSp to maintain genuine business purposes: actual employees, meaningful board/partner decision-making in Luxembourg, and operational risk management for the shipyard's vessel construction, procurement, and financing activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False Declaration of SCSp Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately allocating no or understated shipyard profit to partners, booking fictitious construction costs, or hiding revenue from an Ocean Container Vessel Shipyard contract in an offshore escrow account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment at 24.94% with late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years for evasion of Luxembourg corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the general partner who sign or approve false allocations are jointly and severally liable for evaded corporate tax, interest, and penalties; corporate veil is pierced and courts may impose asset freezes, travel bans, and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a mere mailbox entity: no real Luxembourg decision-making, no operating shipyard assets in jurisdiction, no employees, and transfers of profits to a non-resident partner solely to achieve tax transparency benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp's transparent tax status, retroactive assessment at 24.94%, denial of participation exemption and DTA treaty benefits, plus fines under the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and ultimate beneficial owners are jointly assessed on the reclassified profit; where the unpaid tax balance exceeds EUR 250,000, courts routinely issue travel bans and freezing orders against directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the SCSp beneficial-owner details in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), facilitating cash or crypto payments over EUR 10,000 for ship components, or allowing an undisclosed non-resident principal to control vessel sale escrow accounts without KYC evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory penalty up to EUR 500,000 and confiscation of the proceeds of the ship sale; if the matter is prosecuted as financing of serious crime, the criminal fine can reach EUR 1,250,000 with imprisonment for the responsible manager.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly fail to file the RBE or who authorise unvetted escrow brownouts may be held civilly liable for loss and suffer disqualification, travel restrictions, and imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing the SCSp's shipyard at a non-arm's-length price (e.g., selling container vessels to a related party below cost, paying excessive group-management or IP fees to a non-resident affiliate, or creating circular LC payments to shift profit).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Correction of taxable income under Luxembourg law (Articles 56/164 LIR), additional assessment at 24.94%, late-payment interest, and a penalty of up to 10% of the adjusted amount; double taxation is not relieved if documentation is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false transfer pricing declarations or creating fictitious invoices are personally liable for restitution of the tax shortfall and may be prosecuted for tax fraud, with criminal fines and jail terms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a non-resident limited partner an accelerated distribution before the completion of a maritime construction LC, or stripping the SCSp of capital while leaving the shipyard with unpaid creditors and no legal reserve.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax at 15% assessed on the distribution, invalidation of the distribution vis-à-vis creditors, and personal liability of the general partner to restore funds under Luxembourg partnership law; fines can reach EUR 75,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner managers are personally liable to third-party creditors for unlawful distributions and face civil restitution orders, provisional attachment of personal assets, and restriction from managing commercial companies.
